sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah reveals the three aspects of the repentance of Yom Kippur: the change in revealed soul powers, the drawing down of a new will from Ein Sof, and the essential bond of the soul's essence with the Awtsmoos.

translations.translation: And this is: "In sukkot you shall dwell... every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot... for I caused the children of Israel to dwell in sukkot..."
For "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot" and "for I caused [them] to dwell in sukkot" are two reasons for "in sukkot you shall dwell"
(as explained in the maamar of the continuum of Rosh Hashanah 5703,
cited above in section 2).
And the concept is,
that "in sukkot you shall dwell" is the revelation of the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,
and in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,
there are three matters.
The teshuvah itself,
and two matters in the root and cause of teshuvah.
For the teshuvah itself
(even the teshuvah of Yom Kippur)
is that a person changes himself,
that he leaves his previous existence and becomes a new existence.
For this change is in the revealed powers of the soul.
And this change in the revealed powers of the person is by his arousing and revealing the essence of the soul within him,
namely the essence of the soul that is related to the revealed powers.
[And similarly, regarding Above,
that the person becomes pleasing before Him as before the sin,
is
because through teshuvah a new will is drawn from Ein Sof, the Master of Will.]
And there is another matter in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,
that is felt in it in revelation,
that the root and true cause of teshuvah is the bond of the essence of the soul
(which is above relation to the revealed powers)
with the Awtsmoos
(which is above the Master of Will).
Therefore,
also in the matter of "in sukkot you shall dwell"
(which is the revelation of the teshuvah of Yom Kippur),
there are three matters.
The matter of "in sukkot you shall dwell" itself – the change in the proximate encompassing [light],
that it becomes a settled light.
And the reason for this is – "for I caused [them] to dwell in sukkot" in the manner of an arousal from Above.
And it can be said,
that it is similar to what was brought above in section 6, that this, that through an arousal from below the revealed will is aroused
(even though the arousal from below is incomparable relative to the will)
is not from the perspective of the revealed will itself
(for since the revealed will relates to worlds, it is defined by the fact that creations are incomparable relative to it and they cannot arouse it),
but rather because it is so determined in the absolute will.
And similarly, in the matter of "in sukkot you shall dwell",
the change, so to speak, that occurs in the proximate encompassing [light] to become a settled light is,
because "for I caused [them] to dwell in sukkot" in the manner of an arousal from Above,
a drawing from the Essence of Ein Sof, regarding which there is no distinction between encompassing and internal, and even the encompassing can come into settlement.
[Similar to how through teshuvah a will
(new)
is drawn from Ein Sof, the Master of Will.]
And there is another reason for "in sukkot you shall dwell" – "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot",
in the distant encompassing [light].
For the matter of dwelling
(settlement)
in the distant encompassing is not in the manner of an action
[for in the distant encompassing,
the level of "not a man",
action and change cannot apply,
as above in section 3],
but rather that "every native-born Jew"
"shall dwell in sukkot"
(the distant encompassing)
from their own side,
because they are rooted in the Awtsmoos.
[And this is what our sages, of blessed memory, said
on the verse "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot": it teaches that all of Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah,
for at this level all of Israel are equal.]
And it is similar to the matter of the essence of Yom Kippur,
that from the perspective of the essential bond of the essence of the soul with the Awtsmoos, there is no defect from the outset.
And just as on Yom Kippur,
the matter of its essence shines in revelation also in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,
that in the teshuvah of Yom Kippur it is felt
(as above)
that it is drawn from the essential bond of the essence of the soul with the Awtsmoos,
so too is it in Sukkot,
that "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot" is a reason for "in sukkot you shall dwell",
that this, that the proximate encompassing is drawn into inwardness and becomes a settled light,
is felt in it,
that the reason for this is "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkot",
in the distant encompassing,
the essential bond of the essence of the soul with the Awtsmoos.
